title: Chicken Fajitas
subtitle: Spiced chicken strips with peppers in warm tortillas
excerpt: Chicken breast strips marinated in lime and spices, cooked with peppers and onion in a very hot pan, served in warm flour tortillas with soured cream and guacamole.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fajitas originate in Tex-Mex cooking from the ranches of southern Texas, where cheaper cuts of beef such as skirt steak were grilled over an open fire. Chicken fajitas became popular in the UK during the 1990s and became one of the most widely cooked weeknight meals. The essential elements are the same: marinated protein, high-heat cooking to get colour and char, and the filling served in warm tortillas at the table.

recipeTools.notes: The pan must be very hot to get colour on the chicken.

content.text: The pan must be very hot before the chicken goes in: moderate heat gives grey, steamed chicken rather than coloured, slightly charred strips. Cook in batches if needed so the pan is not crowded. Warm the tortillas in the oven or briefly in a dry frying pan. The filling should sizzle when it hits the pan.

Mix 2 tablespoons of olive oil, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, chilli powder, and salt together. Toss the chicken strips in the marinade. Leave for at least 15 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the fridge.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large frying pan over very high heat until smoking. Cook the chicken strips in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until coloured and cooked through. Remove and keep warm.
Add the peppers and onion to the same pan. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes over high heat until softened and beginning to char at the edges.
Return the chicken to the pan. Toss together for 1 minute. Serve in warm tortillas with coriander, soured cream, and any other toppings.
